decisions.quote: Experimental Economics Replication Project Replication of Reference Points and Effort Provision by Abeler, J./Falk, A./Goette, L./Huffman, D. (2011) in: The American Economic Review, 101(2), pp. 470–492. Replication Authors: Felix Holzmeister, Jürgen Huber, Michael Kirchler and Michael Razen Abeler et al. find that in a real effort task, effort provision and earnings are higher if the expectations-based reference point is high ( hi treatment) compared to low (lo treatment).
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Abeler et al., 2011), header and introduction (line 1277); also Reference 33 (lines 286-287) and Table S2 (lines 1139-1142)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 0 identify the same tested original study: Abeler, Falk, Goette, and Huffman (2011), 'Reference Points and Effort Provision', American Economic Review 101(2), 470-492.

decisions.quote: Given the criteria and procedure outlined above, the hypothesis of interest has not been replicated at a significance level of α < 5%. The relative effect size equals 36.04% and the p-value of the hypothesis test is 0.160.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Abeler et al., 2011), Discussion (line 1277); corroborated by Table S1 (line 1255)
decisions.reason: In the individual primary replication report for Abeler et al. (2011), the OLS treatment difference in effort provision between the hi and lo treatments is non-significant (coefficient = 0.667, p = 0.160, relative effect size = 36.04%), all subsample and temperature-controlled checks are also non-significant, and the authors explicitly conclude that the hypothesis of interest was not replicated (Table S1 also records 'Replicated = No').

decisions.quote: The replication procedure is identical to that of the original study, with the only unavoidable deviation that the replication will be performed at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, in 2015, on students from the University of Innsbruck, whereas the original data was gathered at the University of Bonn, Germany, in 2007, on students from the University of Bonn.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Abeler et al., 2011), Differences from Original Study (line 1277)
decisions.reason: The study collected new experimental data in an independent sample of 318 students at the University of Innsbruck to re-test the published finding of Abeler et al. (2011), which is a replication under the codebook.

corrected_value.title: The Economics of Credence Goods: An Experiment on the Role of Liability, Verifiability, Reputation, and Competition

decisions.quote: Experimental Economics Replication Project Replication of The Economics of Credence Goods: An Experiment on the Role of Liability, Verifiability, Reputation and Competition by Dulleck, U./Kerschbamer,R./Sutter,M. (2011) in: The American Economic Review, 101(2), pp. 526–555. Replication Authors: Anna Dreber, Siri Isaksson and Magnus Johannesson Dulleck et al. study the determinants for efficiency in markets for credence goods.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Dulleck et al., 2011), header and introduction (line 1307); also Reference 40 (lines 299-301) and Table S2 (lines 1166-1168)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped row and blind target 7 identify the same tested original study: Dulleck, Kerschbamer, and Sutter (2011), 'The Economics of Credence Goods: An Experiment on the Role of Liability, Verifiability, Reputation, and Competition', American Economic Review 101(2), 526-555.

decisions.quote: Our replication finds that efficiency is 0.10 in the b/v treatment and 0.71 in the b/lv treatment. This difference is significant using the same test as in the original study (p < 0.001). Thus we replicate the result that liability increases the efficiency in a credence goods market with verifiability. The effect size estimated as the difference between the two treatments is 0.61 (0.71 − 0.10), and the relative effect size of the replication is thus 93.85% (0.61/0.65).
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Dulleck et al., 2011), Replication Results (line 1307); corroborated by Discussion (line 1307) and Table S1 (line 1262)
decisions.reason: In the individual primary replication report for Dulleck et al. (2011), efficiency increases from 0.10 in the b/v treatment to 0.71 in the b/lv treatment (p < 0.001, relative effect size = 93.85%), and the authors explicitly conclude that the original result is replicated (Table S1 also records 'Replicated = Yes').

decisions.quote: The sample for replication consists of 128 students (8 sessions à 2 groups of 8 participants each) at the Goethe University Frankfurt in Germany. We will recruit students who are Bachelor students in business administration and/or economics, and if needed the recruitment will be extended to firstly masters students in economics and/or business and secondly to bachelor students in other fields.
decisions.location: Primary Project Replication Report (Dulleck et al., 2011), Sample (line 1307)
decisions.reason: The study collected new experimental data in a fresh sample of 128 students at Goethe University Frankfurt to re-test the published finding of Dulleck et al. (2011), which is a replication under the codebook.
